chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) used to say to his sons: 'O my sons! Look upon the House of your Lord, so that it should not be empty of you, so that you should not be argued with (or lose out/miss out).'

key_terms.بَيْتَ رَبِّكُمْ: The House of your Lord (referring to the Kaaba)
key_terms.فَلَا تُنَاظَرُوا: So that you are not argued with/disputed (implying steadfastness in devotion)
key_terms.فَلَا يَخْلُوَنَّ مِنْكُمْ: So that it is not empty of you (indicating frequent visitation)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali advise his sons regarding visiting the Kaaba?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) instructs his sons to ensure the Kaaba is never empty of their presence, emphasizing the virtue of constant vigilance (*muraqabah*) in worship. The phrase 'so that you should not be argued with' (*la tunaẓarū*) signifies that consistent devotion serves as irrefutable evidence of one's piety, silencing any potential detractors or doubts regarding their spiritual commitment. This advice underscores the Shia emphasis on the Kaaba not merely as a destination, but as a focal point for maintaining an unbroken spiritual tether to the Divine.
